```ts
import pino, { type Logger, type LoggerOptions } from "pino";
import pinoPretty from "pino-pretty";

export type { Logger };

const EMAIL = /[A-Z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Z0-9.-]+\.[A-Z]{2,}/gi;
const IPV4 = /\b(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}\b/g;
// Full form, compressed form with "::", and leading "::" form. Requires "::" or 8 groups so times like 10:30:45 are untouched.
const IPV6 = /(?:[0-9a-f]{1,4}:){7}[0-9a-f]{1,4}|(?:[0-9a-f]{1,4}:){1,7}:(?:[0-9a-f]{1,4}(?::[0-9a-f]{1,4}){0,6})?|::(?:[0-9a-f]{1,4}(?::[0-9a-f]{1,4}){0,6})/gi;
// phone, and to (the field Vonage takes the number in, and the mailer its address), keep a phone number out of every log line (1b design, section 10).
const SECRET_KEYS = new Set(["authorization", "cookie", "set-cookie", "password", "token", "secret", "session", "code", "otp", "phone", "to"]);

/**
 * A failed query as drizzle-orm wraps the driver's error: its message is "Failed query: <statement>", a line feed, and
 * "params: " with every parameter of the statement. Those are what a request wrote (a staff text with its salt, a
 * notifier's explanation, an account id), and they must not outlive their erasure in a log (3c design, section 11,
 * Privacy). Such an error is logged by its statement, and by the code, the constraint and the message of the database's
 * own error, which name no value; its stack keeps its frames.
 */
const FAILED_QUERY = "Failed query: ";
const PARAMS_FROM = String.fromCharCode(10) + "params: ";

function failedQuery(err: Error): Record<string, unknown> | null {
  const at = err.message.indexOf(PARAMS_FROM);
  if (!err.message.startsWith(FAILED_QUERY) || at === -1) return null;
  const message = err.message.slice(0, at);
  // The frames are the stack's last lines that start with "at": the message above them, parameters included, is dropped.
  const lines = (err.stack ?? "").split(String.fromCharCode(10));
  let first = lines.length;
  while (first > 0 && lines[first - 1]!.trimStart().startsWith("at ")) first--;
  const stack = [`${err.name}: ${message}`, ...lines.slice(first)].join(String.fromCharCode(10));
  const cause = (err as { cause?: unknown }).cause;
  const db = cause && typeof cause === "object" ? (cause as { code?: unknown; constraint_name?: unknown; message?: unknown }) : null;
  return {
    name: err.name,
    message: scrub(message),
    stack: scrub(stack),
    ...(typeof db?.code === "string" ? { code: db.code } : {}),
    ...(typeof db?.constraint_name === "string" ? { constraint: db.constraint_name } : {}),
    ...(typeof db?.message === "string" ? { cause: scrub(db.message) } : {}),
  };
}

/** Recursively masks emails, IPs, and secret-bearing keys, and a failed query's parameters. Applied to every log line. */
export function scrub(value: unknown, key?: string): unknown {
  if (key && SECRET_KEYS.has(key.toLowerCase())) return "[redacted]";
  if (typeof value === "string") return value.replace(EMAIL, "[email]").replace(IPV6, "[ip]").replace(IPV4, "[ip]");
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map((v) => scrub(v));
  if (value && typeof value === "object" && !(value instanceof Error)) {
    const out: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) out[k] = scrub(v, k);
    return out;
  }
  if (value instanceof Error) return failedQuery(value) ?? { name: value.name, message: scrub(value.message), stack: value.stack === undefined ? undefined : scrub(value.stack) };
  return value;
}

export function createLogger(level: string, pretty = false): Logger {
  const options: LoggerOptions = {
    level,
    base: undefined,
    formatters: { log: (obj) => scrub(obj) as Record<string, unknown> },
    hooks: {
      logMethod(args, method) {
        const scrubbed = args.map((a) => (typeof a === "string" ? scrub(a) : a));
        return method.apply(this, scrubbed as Parameters<typeof method>);
      },
    },
  };
  // pino-pretty is used as an in-process stream, not a transport: transports spawn a
  // worker thread that needs __dirname, which does not exist inside the bundle.
  return pretty ? pino(options, pinoPretty({ colorize: true })) : pino(options);
}
```

```ts
import { ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { FlatTemplateName, MailMessage, NoticeUpdateData } from "./mailer";

export interface RenderedMail {
  subject: string;
  text: string;
  html: string;
}

const ESCAPES: Record<string, string> = { "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;", "'": "&#39;" };

function escapeHtml(value: string): string {
  return value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (ch) => ESCAPES[ch]!);
}

function need(data: Record<string, string>, key: string): string {
  const value = data[key];
  if (value === undefined || value === "") throw new Error(`mail template data is missing "${key}"`);
  return value;
}

/** Plain paragraphs only: no images, no tracking, no anchor tags. URLs appear as text. */
function build(subject: string, paragraphs: string[]): RenderedMail {
  return {
    subject,
    text: `${paragraphs.join("\n\n")}\n`,
    html: `<!doctype html><html><body style="font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;line-height:1.5">${paragraphs
      .map((p) => `<p>${escapeHtml(p)}</p>`)
      .join("")}</body></html>`,
  };
}

/**
 * The subject of the statement's mail, by the decision's kind and outcome (3c design, section 7.15). The moderation
 * module names one of these keys; the words are written here only, so no caller passes a subject of its own.

        "Your korbat account was deleted as you asked, and your handle stays reserved so nobody can take it.",
        ACCOUNT_DELETION_WORDS,
        "This cannot be undone. Thank you for having been part of korbat; you are welcome back with a new account any time.",
      ]);
    case "passkey_added":
      // The link runs the lockdown anchored at the passkey's creation (1c design, section 7.6): it reaches back a day,
      // so a password or two-factor set up just before the passkey, from the same stolen session, goes with it.
      return build("A passkey was added to your korbat account", [
        `A passkey named "${need(data, "name")}" was added to your korbat account from ${need(data, "deviceLabel")} at ${need(data, "time")}.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do.",
        `If this was not you, open this link within 7 days. It removes this passkey, signs out every session, removes your password, and turns off every passkey and two-factor authentication set up since the day before this one was added; then you sign in with a code sent to this address: ${need(data, "removeUrl")}`,
      ]);
    case "passkey_removed":
      return build("A passkey was removed from your korbat account", [
        `The passkey named "${need(data, "name")}" was removed from your korbat account at ${need(data, "time")}. It can no longer sign in.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, sign in, open Security, and review your passkeys, sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "passkey_suspect":
      // A counter that went backwards (1c design, section 2): the signature was right, so someone holds the key, and
      // either the authenticator was cloned or a backup was restored. Only the owner can tell, so the key stays off.
      return build("A passkey on your korbat account was switched off", [
        `A sign-in just used what looks like a copy of your passkey named "${need(data, "name")}", so korbat switched that passkey off. It can no longer sign in.`,
        "Sign in with a code sent to this address, open Security, remove it and add a new one. If you did not try to sign in just now, also review your sessions and devices.",
      ]);
    case "recovery_code_used":
      // A code spent at re-authentication (1c design, section 7.2): each of the ten works once, so the owner should know the count is down.
      return build("A recovery code was used on your korbat account", [
        "A recovery code was just used to confirm it's you on your korbat account. Each code works once; set up two-factor authentication again from Security to get a new set.",
        "If this was not you, sign in, open Security, sign out everywhere and set up two-factor authentication again.",
      ]);
    case "staff_key_added":
      return staffMail("A staff key was added to your korbat staff account", [
        `A staff key named "${need(data, "name")}" was registered for your korbat staff account at ${need(data, "time")}. It can open the staff console.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, tell the operator at once; they revoke the key with the staff command line.",
      ]);
    case "staff_session_started":
      return staffMail("A staff session started on the korbat console", [
        `A staff session was started on the korbat console at ${need(data, "time")} with your staff key "${need(data, "name")}", from ${need(data, "browser")}.`,
        "If this was you, there is nothing to do. If not, someone holds that key: tell the operator at once; they revoke it and every session it opened with the staff command line.",
      ]);
    case "staff_key_suspect":

      // app's Security screen; only the operator can enrol a replacement.

        `A use of your staff key "${need(data, "name")}" on the korbat console (a sign-in or a confirmation) looked like a copy of it, so korbat switched that key off and ended every staff session it opened. It can no longer open the console.`,
        "Ask the operator for a link to register a new key. If you did not use it just now, tell them so: someone else holds a copy of the key.",

      return staffMail("Staff keys revoked on your korbat staff account", [
        `These staff keys of your korbat staff account were revoked at ${need(data, "time")}: ${need(data, "names")}. They can no longer open the console, and every staff session they opened has ended.`,
        "If you expected this, there is nothing to do. If not, ask the operator why.",

      // The receipt of a report or a notice (3c design, section 7.15). `items` is the list of korbat links the report
      // named, as the sender joins them: built from parsed ids, an account's from the handle as it was named. With
      // `pageUrl` it goes to a signed-out notifier's address, and the link's fragment holds that contact's mail token,
      // which no server log sees; without it, to an account, whose reports are in the app.
      return userMail(`korbat received your report ${need(data, "ref")}`, [
        RECEIPT.received(need(data, "ref"), need(data, "time"), need(data, "items")),
        "A moderator decides each item that names something on korbat; a link that names nothing is answered automatically. You get one email with every decision, at most once a day.",
        data.pageUrl ? RECEIPT.page(data.pageUrl) : "You can follow it in korbat under Settings, Cases, Your reports.",

      // subject is a key of the table above, and `statement` holds the statement's paragraphs, one per line, exactly as
      // statementParagraphs rendered them: the author's screen and the console's preview show the same words.
      const key = need(data, "subject");
      if (!Object.hasOwn(DECISION_MAIL_SUBJECTS, key)) throw new Error(`mail template data holds a subject that the statement's mail does not have: "${key}"`);
      const lines = need(data, "statement")
        .split("\n")
        .filter((paragraph) => paragraph.trim() !== "");

      // case is its own oldest, so its sentence gives one time and is worded for one.
      const lane = "in the urgent lane (child sexual abuse or exploitation, direct threats, violence, public security or self-harm)";
      return staffMail("korbat: a case is waiting in the urgent lane", [
        need(data, "count") === "1" ? `1 case ${lane} is waiting, since ${need(data, "oldest")}.` : `${need(data, "count")} cases ${lane} are waiting; the oldest since ${need(data, "oldest")}.`,

      // there only for a lane with such a case; a single case is its own oldest and is worded as one.
      const lines: string[] = [];

        lines.push(count === "1" ? `${lane.name}: 1 case waiting longer than ${lane.time}, since ${oldest}.` : `${lane.name}: ${count} cases waiting longer than ${lane.time}; the oldest since ${oldest}.`);

        lines.push(
          held === "1"
            ? "1 case has held a measure taken while deciding for more than 24 hours; its author cannot appeal until the case is decided."

      if (lines.length === 0) throw new Error("mail template data for moderation_waiting names nothing that waits");
      return staffMail("korbat: cases are waiting longer than their response time", [...lines, "Open the staff console. Until the phone alerts of sub-project 3e, this email is the only reminder."]);

        `The staff account ${who} confirmed ${need(data, "count")} decisions in the last 15 minutes.`,
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not confirm them, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,

      // account is told at once. It names the staff account and the time, never the case or its author.
      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;

Nobody at korbat could open those images while they were protected.",
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not confirm it, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,

A seal for good is lifted only on the answer of the authority korbat reported the images to, and a seal taken while deciding only when it was taken in error: the operator compares this decision with their R2 records. If it was not expected, ask them; if their key may be in someone else's hands, the operator revokes it with staff.js revoke, and whoever is on duty opens a finding citing R2 on the post or the account and seals its images while deciding.",
      ]);
    }

      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;
      return staffMail("korbat: a staff account reached its daily case limit", [
        `The staff account ${who} opened ${need(data, "limit")} different cases today and cannot open others until midnight UTC.`,
        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not open them, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,

      const who = `@${need(data, "handle")}`;

        `Every staff account gets this email. If ${who} is your account and you did not reveal it, someone else holds your key: tell the operator at once.`,

}

const OUTSIDE_KORBAT = "go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";

/**
 * The daily update of decisions on a person's reports (3c design, section 7.15), the one template whose data is a
 * structure. In this order: each receipt the 24-hour cap folded, with its page link, and after them once where korbat
 * says how it handles reports; one paragraph for each line; for a signed-out reader the page of each notice the update
 * has a line for; and, only when it carries a line, that nothing was automated, how to ask for a re-examination, what is
 * final within korbat, what to do about a wrong link, and the courts and the Digital Services Coordinator. Every
 * sentence is chosen from the lines' fields alone, and a line's outcome is printed as the moderation module composed it.
 */
export function renderNoticeUpdate(data: NoticeUpdateData): RenderedMail {
  const { lines, receipts, pages } = data;
  if (lines.length === 0 && receipts.length === 0) throw new Error("mail template data for notice_update holds nothing to tell: no line and no receipt");
  // An account's reports are followed in the app: its update never carries a link with a token.
  if (data.signedIn && (receipts.length > 0 || pages.length > 0)) throw new Error("mail template data for a signed-in notice_update holds a receipt or a page link");
  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const receipt of receipts) out.push(RECEIPT.received(receipt.ref, receipt.time, receipt.items), RECEIPT.page(receipt.pageUrl));
  if (receipts.length > 0) {
    if (!data.termsUrl) throw new Error('mail template data is missing "termsUrl"');
    out.push(RECEIPT.terms(data.termsUrl));
  }
  for (const line of lines) {
    // The outcome's words end in their own full stop.
    const outcome = line.outcome.endsWith(".") ? line.outcome : `${line.outcome}.`;
    out.push(`${line.ref}, item ${line.item} (${line.link})${line.reexamination ? ", re-examined" : ""}: ${outcome}`);
  }
  for (const page of pages) out.push(`To see report ${page.ref} or ask for a re-examination of a decision on it, open this page: ${page.pageUrl}`);
  if (lines.length > 0) {
    const automatic = lines.some((line) => line.automatic);
    out.push(`No automated means were used to decide${automatic ? ", except for links found to name nothing on korbat, which were checked automatically" : ""}.`);
    const reexaminable = lines.some((line) => line.reexaminable);
    if (reexaminable) {
      out.push(
        `You can ask korbat once, within six months and free of charge, to re-examine a moderator's decision to take no action: it is decided again as a new report. ${
          data.signedIn ? "Use korbat's Settings, Cases, Your reports." : "Use the page linked in this email for that report."
        }`,
      );
    }
    // An answer given while nobody could open the images leaves the re-examination unspent, so it is never called final.
    if (lines.some((line) => line.changed || (line.reexamination && !line.unseen))) out.push("A decision changed on review or by a correction, or given on re-examination, is final within korbat.");
    if (automatic) out.push("If a link was wrong, send a new report with the right link.");
    out.push(`You can ${reexaminable ? "also " : ""}${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`);
  }
  return userMail(lines.length > 0 ? "Decisions on your reports to korbat" : "korbat received your reports", out);
}

/** A message as it is sent: the structured template by its own renderer, every other by renderTemplate. */
export function renderMail(message: MailMessage): RenderedMail {
  return message.template === "notice_update" ? renderNoticeUpdate(message.data) : renderTemplate(message.template, message.data);
}

/**
 * A moderation mail to a user: plain paragraphs as every mail, closed by the sentence that korbat's staff ask for
 * nothing by mail, so a message that asks for a password or a code, or for an answer, is known for a fake (3c design,
 * section 7.15).
 */
function userMail(subject: string, paragraphs: string[]): RenderedMail {
  return build(subject, [...paragraphs, "korbat staff never ask for your password or a code, and korbat does not read replies to this email."]);
}

/**
 * A staff mail: plain paragraphs as every mail, closed by the sentence that no staff mail carries a link, so a message
 * that does carry one is known for a fake (3a design, section 7).
 */
function staffMail(subject: string, paragraphs: string[]): RenderedMail {
  return build(subject, [...paragraphs, "korbat never puts a link in a staff email."]);
}
```

```ts
import type { MediaSize } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { VARIANTS } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import type { MediaDeps } from "./context";
import type { StoredFile } from "./files";
import { owedLate, requestOwed } from "./owed";
import type { CaseReach, HeldImage, HoldPair } from "./repo";
import { RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHANS } from "./sweeper";
import { WEBP_HEADER_BYTES, webpSize } from "./webp";

/**
 * How many image rows one call of dropDisposable deletes at most: half of what the reconcile pass deletes without
 * MEDIA_RECONCILE=force. The files of a batch are requested after its commit; a batch notes inside its transaction that
 * they are owed, so a crash in between, or a request that cannot be written, loses nothing: the note is what the request
 * is written from later. Should the notes be lost as well (an uploads volume put back from an older copy), one batch's
 * files, with other deletions' lost in the same way, still stay within what one reconcile pass removes by itself (3c
 * design, section 5).
 */
export const DISPOSAL_BATCH = RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHANS / 2;

/** An image file opened for staff, with the post it is on. The caller reads the handle from its start and closes it. */
export interface StaffImage {
  postId: string;
  file: StoredFile;
}

/**
 * What the moderation module needs from this one (3c design, section 5). The moderation module never names an image
 * row: it hands over its transaction, its cases and its targets, and gets back what its evidence lists and what its
 * screens count.
 */
export interface MediaForCases {
  /**
   * An intake's holds, inside its transaction: each pair `{ caseId, postId }` locks the post's image rows and places
   * the case's evidence hold on them; a pair `{ ownerId }` only locks every image row on that account's posts, for a
   * report of child sexual abuse material about the account. All rows are locked by one statement, in one id order.
   * It answers each post pair's images in position order, for the post's snapshot; an empty list means they are gone.
   */
  hold(tx: DbTx, pairs: readonly HoldPair[]): Promise<Map<string, HeldImage[]>>;
  /**
   * Opens an image file for staff, or answers null: the only function that does (gate V; 3c design, sections 6.1 and
   * 7.3). Never an image of a frozen post, a sealed image or an erased one, on whatever case the request came; and only a
   * file whose header says that it is a WebP of the size its variant and its row allow.
   */
  staffImage(mediaId: string, size: MediaSize): Promise<StaffImage | null>;
  /** What a case about this post or account reaches: counts, a day and a time, never an id, an alt text or a file. */
  reach(target: { type: "post" | "account"; id: string }): Promise<CaseReach>;
  /**
   * Deletes, in the caller's transaction, at most DISPOSAL_BATCH image rows that nothing retains and that their post's
   * deletion, their owner's purge or an erasure left behind, the lowest ids first, and answers their ids. Still inside
   * that transaction it notes that their files are owed a request: where the note cannot be written this throws, the
   * transaction fails, and no row is gone whose files could not be found again. The caller asks for the files with
   * requestDeletion after its commit, and calls again until fewer than a batch came back.
   */
  dropDisposable(tx: DbTx): Promise<string[]>;
  /**
   * How many erasures of images are late: the rows the disposal should have taken more than a day ago, and the files of
   * rows that are gone whose request has been owed for longer than a round of the retention job.
   */
  overdueDeletions(): Promise<number>;
  /**
   * Asks the worker to delete the files of these images, and settles what was owed for them. Called after the commit of
   * the transaction that deleted their rows. When it throws, the deletion stays owed.
   */
  requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * Asks again for the files of every row that is gone and whose request was never written, whoever deleted the row
   * (a batch of the disposal, or the account's purge), and answers how many are still owed afterwards. The disposal calls
   * it before its first batch of a round and takes none while the answer is not zero.
   */
  requestOwed(): Promise<number>;
}

/**
 * The moderation module's interface over this module's dependencies, as createMedia hands it out; the tests build it the
 * same way. The clock is read only for the age of what is owed; without one it is the machine's.
 */
export function mediaForCases(deps: Pick<MediaDeps, "repo" | "files" | "log"> & { now?: () => Date }): MediaForCases {
  const nowMs = () => (deps.now?.() ?? new Date()).getTime();

  /**
   * Why a file of the store is not the image its row describes, or null when it is. The store is written by the worker,
   * which runs the decoder, so the bytes are not trusted: the console is given a file only when its first bytes are those
   * of a WebP whose longer side fits the variant, and whose large variant is exactly as large as the row says.
   */
  async function fault(file: StoredFile, size: MediaSize, row: { width: number | null; height: number | null }): Promise<string | null> {
    const head = Buffer.alloc(WEBP_HEADER_BYTES);
    // Read at an explicit position, which leaves the handle's own position at the start for whoever streams the file.
    const { bytesRead } = await file.handle.read(head, 0, WEBP_HEADER_BYTES, 0);
    const stated = webpSize(head.subarray(0, bytesRead));
    if (!stated) return "not a WebP file";
    if (Math.max(stated.width, stated.height) > VARIANTS[size].edge) return "larger than its variant may be";
    if (size === "large" && (stated.width !== row.width || stated.height !== row.height)) return "not the size its row states";
    return null;
  }

  return {
    hold: (tx, pairs) => deps.repo.hold(tx, pairs),

    async staffImage(mediaId, size) {
      const access = await deps.repo.staffAccess(mediaId);
      if (!access || access.status !== "ready") return null;
      // Gate V. The image's state is asked for by name: a state this reader has not been taught opens nothing.
      const shown = access.mediaState === "visible" || access.mediaState === "withheld" || access.mediaState === "removed";
      if (!shown || access.frozen || access.erased) return null;
      const file = await deps.files.openImage(mediaId, size);
      if (!file) return null;
      let reason: string | null;
      try {
        reason = await fault(file, size, access);
      } catch (err) {
        await file.handle.close();
        throw err;
      }
      if (reason !== null) {
        await file.handle.close();
        deps.log.error({ id: mediaId, size, reason }, "media store: refused to open for staff a file that is not the image its row describes");
        return null;
      }
      return { postId: access.postId, file };
    },

    reach: (target) => deps.repo.reach(target),
    async dropDisposable(tx) {
      const ids = await deps.repo.dropDisposable(tx, DISPOSAL_BATCH);
      await deps.files.oweDeletion(ids);
      return ids;
    },
    overdueDeletions: async () => (await deps.repo.overdueDeletions()) + (await owedLate(deps, nowMs())),
    async requestDeletion(ids) {
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(ids);
      await deps.files.settleOwed(ids);
    },
    requestOwed: async () => (await requestOwed(deps, nowMs())).owed,
  };
}
```

```ts
import { constants } from "node:fs";
import { lstat, mkdir, open, readdir, rename, rm, stat, statfs, type FileHandle } from "node:fs/promises";
import path from "node:path";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { MediaSize } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { Heartbeat, MAX_RESULT_BYTES, MAX_VARIANT_BYTES, ResultFile, SNIFF_BYTES, isMediaId, storeLayout, uploadsLayout } from "@korbat/media-protocol";
import { MediaError } from "./context";

/**
 * The API's side of the file protocol (section 2.2 of the 2b design). The API writes the uploads
 * volume and only reads the store volume, which belongs to the worker. The worker runs the image
 * decoder, so everything in the store is treated as written by an attacker: a file is opened first
 * and the open handle is checked afterwards, which leaves no gap between the check and the use.
 */

export interface StoredFile {
  handle: FileHandle;
  size: number;
}

export interface MediaFilesOptions {
  uploadsDir: string;
  storeDir: string;
  log: Logger;
  /** Tests only: pretend the store lives on this device. */
  storeDevice?: number;
}

/**

 * check still holds there), and never waits: opening a FIFO planted in the store would otherwise block a
 * thread of the pool until a writer appeared.

const READ_FLAGS = constants.O_RDONLY | (constants.O_NOFOLLOW ?? 0) | (constants.O_NONBLOCK ?? 0);

export function createMediaFiles(options: MediaFilesOptions) {
  const uploads = uploadsLayout(options.uploadsDir);
  const store = storeLayout(options.storeDir);

   * Opens a file of the store for reading. Returns null unless the open handle is a regular file,
   * on the store's own device, and no larger than `maxBytes`. A symlink to anything outside the
   * volume, /proc/self/environ for one, resolves to another device and is refused here.
   */
  async function openStored(file: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<StoredFile | null> {
    // Looked at before it is opened, so that nothing but a plain file is ever opened; the handle is checked again after.
    try {
      const entry = await lstat(file);
      if (!entry.isFile()) {
        log.error({ file: path.basename(file), directory: entry.isDirectory(), symlink: entry.isSymbolicLink(), fifo: entry.isFIFO() }, "media store: refused an entry that is not a plain file");
        return null;
      }
    } catch (err) {
      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") log.warn({ file: path.basename(file), code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media store: a file could not be inspected");
      return null;
    }
    let handle: FileHandle;
    try {
      handle = await open(file, READ_FLAGS);
    } catch (err) {
      if ((err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== "ENOENT") log.warn({ file: path.basename(file), code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media store: a file could not be opened");
      return null;
    }
    try {
      const stats = await handle.stat();
      if (stats.isFile() && stats.dev === (await device()) && stats.size <= maxBytes) return { handle, size: stats.size };
      log.error({ file: path.basename(file), regular: stats.isFile(), size: stats.size }, "media store: refused a file that is not a plain file of the store");
    } catch (err) {
      log.error({ err }, "media store: could not inspect an open file");
    }
    await handle.close();
    return null;
  }

  async function readStored(file: string, maxBytes: number): Promise<string | null> {
    const stored = await openStored(file, maxBytes);
    if (!stored) return null;
    try {
      return await stored.handle.readFile("utf8");
    } finally {
      await stored.handle.close();
    }
  }

  const namesIn = (dir: string): Promise<string[]> => readdir(dir).catch(() => []);

  return {
    uploads,
    store,

    /** Creates the uploads volume's directories and forgets bodies a crash left half received. */
    async prepare(): Promise<void> {
      await rm(uploads.tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
      for (const dir of [uploads.tmp, uploads.incoming, uploads.deletions, uploads.owed]) await mkdir(dir, { recursive: true });
    },

    /**
     * Streams a request body to tmp/<id>.part. `accept` sees the first bytes before anything is
     * written and throws to refuse them. Bytes are counted here while they arrive, because a
     * declared length can be absent or wrong; one byte over `maxBytes` ends the upload.
     */
    async receive(id: string, body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array> | null, maxBytes: number, accept: (head: Uint8Array) => void): Promise<number> {
      const reader = body?.getReader();
      const first: Uint8Array[] = [];
      let buffered = 0;
      let ended = !reader;
      try {
        while (reader && buffered < SNIFF_BYTES) {
          const chunk = await reader.read();
          if (chunk.done) {
            ended = true;
            break;
          }
          first.push(chunk.value);
          buffered += chunk.value.byteLength;
        }
        accept(Buffer.concat(first).subarray(0, SNIFF_BYTES));
      } catch (err) {
        await reader?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
        throw err;
      }

      const part = uploads.part(id);
      const handle = await open(part, "wx");
      let bytes = 0;
      try {
        const write = async (chunk: Uint8Array) => {
          bytes += chunk.byteLength;
          if (bytes > maxBytes) throw new MediaError("file_too_large", 413);
          await handle.appendFile(chunk);
        };
        for (const chunk of first) await write(chunk);
        while (reader && !ended) {
          const chunk = await reader.read();
          if (chunk.done) break;
          await write(chunk.value);
        }
        await handle.sync();
        await handle.close();
      } catch (err) {
        await reader?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
        await handle.close().catch(() => undefined);
        await rm(part, { force: true });
        throw err;
      }
      return bytes;
    },

    /** The upload becomes visible to the worker. A rename inside one volume is atomic. */
    commit: (id: string): Promise<void> => rename(uploads.part(id), uploads.upload(id)),

    /** Removes an upload, complete or not. A file the worker still holds open on Windows is left for the sweeper. */
    async discardUpload(id: string): Promise<void> {
      for (const file of [uploads.part(id), uploads.upload(id)]) {
        await rm(file, { force: true }).catch((err: unknown) => log.warn({ id, code: (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code }, "media uploads: an upload could not be removed yet"));
      }
    },

    /** The worker's verdict on an upload, or null while there is none. A result that does not parse is ignored and logged. */
    async readResult(id: string): Promise<ResultFile | null> {
      const text = await readStored(store.result(id), MAX_RESULT_BYTES);
      if (text === null) return null;
      try {
        const parsed = ResultFile.safeParse(JSON.parse(text));
        if (parsed.success && parsed.data.id === id) return parsed.data;
      } catch {
        // falls through to the log line below
      }
      log.error({ id }, "media store: ignored a result file that does not follow the protocol");
      return null;
    },

    /** An image file to stream. The caller closes the handle. */
    openImage: (id: string, size: MediaSize): Promise<StoredFile | null> => openStored(store.image(id, size), MAX_VARIANT_BYTES),

    /** Asks the worker to delete images. The request is an empty file named after the id. */
    async requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
      for (const id of ids) await (await open(uploads.deletion(id), "w")).close();
    },

    /**
     * Notes that a request to delete these images is owed: an empty file named after each id, in a directory the worker
     * never reads. Whoever deletes image rows in a transaction writes this inside it, before the commit, and writes the
     * request itself only after the commit: a transaction that does not commit has then asked the worker for nothing
     * (its rows are back, and a report may freeze them the next moment), and a commit whose request is lost or cannot
     * be written leaves the note, from which the request is written later. Where the note cannot be written this throws,
     * the caller's transaction fails with it, and no row goes whose files could not be found again.
     */
    async oweDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
      for (const id of ids) await (await open(uploads.owedDeletion(id), "w")).close();
    },

    /** The deletions that are owed, each with the age of its note. */
    async owedDeletions(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      for (const id of (await namesIn(uploads.owed)).filter(isMediaId)) {
        const stats = await stat(uploads.owedDeletion(id)).catch(() => null);
        if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
      }
      return found;
    },

    /** Removes the notes of these ids: their request stands, or their rows turned out to be kept. */
    async settleOwed(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
      for (const id of ids) await rm(uploads.owedDeletion(id), { force: true });
    },

    /** Ids with a deletion request. */
    async deletionRequests(): Promise<string[]> {
      return (await namesIn(uploads.deletions)).filter(isMediaId);
    },

    /** Deletion requests with their age, for the sweeper, which only withdraws one after a grace period. */
    async deletionRequestAges(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      for (const id of (await namesIn(uploads.deletions)).filter(isMediaId)) {
        const stats = await stat(uploads.deletion(id)).catch(() => null);
        if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
      }
      return found;
    },

    withdrawDeletion: (id: string): Promise<void> => rm(uploads.deletion(id), { force: true }),

    /** Whether the worker still holds anything for this id. */
    async imageRemains(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      for (const target of [store.imageDir(id), store.result(id)]) {
        if (await stat(target).then(() => true, () => false)) return true;
      }
      return false;
    },

    /** Every image folder in the store with its age, for the reconcile pass. */
    async storedImages(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      for (const shard of await namesIn(store.files)) {
        if (!/^[0-9a-f]{2}$/.test(shard)) continue;
        for (const id of await namesIn(path.join(store.files, shard))) {
          if (!isMediaId(id) || !id.startsWith(shard)) continue;
          const stats = await stat(store.imageDir(id)).catch(() => null);
          if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
        }
      }
      return found;
    },

    /** Every upload on disk, complete or partial, with its age, for the reconcile pass. */
    async storedUploads(now: number): Promise<{ id: string; ageMs: number }[]> {
      const found: { id: string; ageMs: number }[] = [];
      const add = async (id: string, file: string) => {
        if (!isMediaId(id)) return;
        const stats = await stat(file).catch(() => null);
        if (stats) found.push({ id, ageMs: now - stats.mtimeMs });
      };
      for (const name of await namesIn(uploads.incoming)) await add(name, path.join(uploads.incoming, name));
      for (const name of await namesIn(uploads.tmp)) if (name.endsWith(".part")) await add(name.slice(0, -".part".length), path.join(uploads.tmp, name));
      return found;
    },

    /** Milliseconds since the worker's last heartbeat, or null when there is none to read. */
    async heartbeatAge(now: number): Promise<number | null> {
      const text = await readStored(store.heartbeat, 1024);
      if (text === null) return null;
      try {
        const beat = Heartbeat.safeParse(JSON.parse(text));
        return beat.success ? now - beat.data.at : null;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    },

    /** Free space on the volume with less of it. The volumes share a disk with Postgres, so running out would stop the database. */
    async freeBytes(): Promise<number> {
      const sizes = await Promise.all([uploads.root, store.root].map(async (dir) => {
        const fs = await statfs(dir);
        return fs.bavail * fs.bsize;
      }));
      return Math.min(...sizes);
    },
  };
}

export type MediaFiles = ReturnType<typeof createMediaFiles>;
```

```ts
 * configuration: its only caller is `staff.js text-verify`, which opens database URLs alone and, like every file outside
 * this module, may not name the image table itself.

export function imageModerationStates(apiDb: Db, afterId: string | null, limit: number): Promise<ImageModerationState[]> {

}

/** What the account module needs from this one (1b design, section 5): the purge of a deleted account's images, and the data export. */
export interface MediaForAccount {
  /**
   * Removes the owner's image rows, on a post or not, whatever their state, inside the account purge's transaction; the
   * ids name the files to delete. A row that a case holds, and every row of a frozen post, stays and is not answered
   * (3c design, section 7.10): the purge asks for the files of the rows it was answered, and of no other. Still inside
   * that transaction it notes that those files are owed a request, so the rows cannot be gone for good without a record
   * from which the request is written; where the note cannot be written this throws, and the purge's transaction fails.
   */
  purgeOwner(tx: DbTx, ownerId: string): Promise<string[]>;
  /**
   * Asks the worker to delete the files of these images, whatever their state: an upload still waiting
   * in the uploads volume is removed first, as the sweeper removes one it gives up on, so no worker picks
   * it up after the account is gone (removing is idempotent, and costs nothing for an image whose upload
   * was taken already); then one empty request file per id, so asking twice is asking once; then what was
   * owed for them is settled. The account purge asks only after its transaction has committed, for the rows
   * that transaction deleted: a request cannot be taken back, and rows that a failed commit put back may be
   * frozen by a report before the purge runs again. When it throws, the deletion stays owed, and the sweeper
   * asks again at its next pass.
   */
  requestDeletion(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<void>;
  /**
   * The account's ready images that it is still shown, on a post or not, each with the checked open of its large
   * variant: the store is written by the worker and not trusted, so a file is read only when it is a plain file of the
   * store's own device no larger than a variant may be, and only up to the size that check measured
   * (null, and the export lists the image as missing, otherwise). A sealed image, an image of a deleted post and an
   * erased one are not listed; `open` reads the row again and answers null for an image that has become one of those
   * since the list was read, so a seal that commits while an archive streams leaves no sealed file in it from then on.

  exportImages(ownerId: string): Promise<{ id: string; open(): Promise<StoredFile | null> }[]>;

/** The account module's interface over this module's dependencies, as createMedia hands it out; the integration tests build it the same way. */
export function mediaForAccount(deps: MediaDeps): MediaForAccount {
  return {
    async purgeOwner(tx, ownerId) {
      const ids = await deps.repo.purgeOwner(tx, ownerId);
      await deps.files.oweDeletion(ids);
      return ids;
    },
    async requestDeletion(ids) {
      for (const id of ids) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(ids);
      await deps.files.settleOwed(ids);

        open: async () => ((await deps.repo.isExportable(ownerId, id)) ? deps.files.openImage(id, "large") : null),

}

export interface CreateMediaOptions {
  /** The korbat_api pool. The module never sees the auth pool. */
  apiDb: Db;
  /** The uploads volume, which the API writes, and the store volume, which it only reads. */
  uploadsDir: string;
  storeDir: string;
  formats: readonly MediaFormat[];
  minFreeBytes: number;
  /** See MEDIA_RECONCILE; defaults to `on`. */
  reconcile?: "on" | "off" | "force";
  logger: Logger;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's resolveSession. The file routes run it themselves, and only when they must. */
  resolveSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** Image requests have their own per-IP bucket in the store the other limits use. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  /** Built from the social module's write limits, so every per-account limit lives in one table. */
  enforceUploadLimit: MediaDeps["enforceUploadLimit"];
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createMedia(options: CreateMediaOptions) {
  const deps: MediaDeps = {
    repo: createMediaRepo(options.apiDb),
    files: createMediaFiles({ uploadsDir: options.uploadsDir, storeDir: options.storeDir, log: options.logger }),
    formats: options.formats,
    minFreeBytes: options.minFreeBytes,
    reconcileMode: options.reconcile ?? "on",
    enforceUploadLimit: options.enforceUploadLimit,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  const forPosts: MediaForPosts = {
    attach: (tx, input) => deps.repo.attach(tx, input),
    detachAll: (tx, postId) => deps.repo.detachAll(tx, postId),
    requestDeletion: (ids) => deps.files.requestDeletion(ids),
    forPosts: (postIds) => deps.repo.forPosts(postIds),
  };
  const forAccount = mediaForAccount(deps);
  const forCases = mediaForCases(deps);
  return {
    deps,
    /** The interface the social module uses to put images on posts and read them back. */
    forPosts,
    /** The interface the account module uses. */
    forAccount,
    /** The interface the moderation module uses: an intake's holds, what a case reaches, the staff's image, the disposal. */
    forCases,
    /** Creates the uploads volume's directories. Call once before serving. */
    prepare: () => deps.files.prepare(),
    routes: mediaRoutes(deps, options.requireSession),
    /** Mounted before the global rate limit and session resolution. */
    fileRoutes: mediaFileRoutes(deps, { resolveSession: options.resolveSession, rateLimitStore: options.rateLimitStore }),
    /** One pass of housekeeping at the given time. The server runs it on a timer; tests call it directly. */
    sweep: (now: Date, options: { reconcile: boolean }) => sweep(deps, now, options),
    /** Starts sweeping every thirty seconds under the shared job lock, and returns the function that stops it. */
    startSweeper: (lock: JobLock) => createSweeper(deps, lock).start(),
    /** An advisory health check: the worker's heartbeat is fresh and the volumes have room. */
    async healthCheck(): Promise<void> {
      const age = await deps.files.heartbeatAge(deps.now().getTime());
      if (age === null || age > HEARTBEAT_STALE_MS) throw new Error("the image worker's heartbeat is missing or stale");
      if ((await deps.files.freeBytes()) < deps.minFreeBytes) throw new Error("free space on the media volumes is under the floor");
    },
  };
}
```

```ts
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { MediaDeps } from "./context";
import { finalize } from "./flows/status";
import { requestOwed } from "./owed";

/** An upload the worker has not answered for this long has failed. Normal processing takes seconds. */
export const PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60_000;
/** An upload nobody put on a post within a day is removed. */
export const UNATTACHED_TTL_MS = 24 * 60 * 60_000;
/** Files without a row are only treated as orphans once they are this old, so work in flight is never touched. */
export const ORPHAN_AGE_MS = 60 * 60_000;
/**
 * A deletion request stays at least this long. The worker may be in the middle of an image when
 * the request arrives, and writes its files afterwards; one image takes at most two minutes before
 * the worker's watchdog ends it, so after ten the request has been seen with everything in place.
 */
export const DELETION_GRACE_MS = 10 * 60_000;
export const SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000;
export const RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * 60_000;
/**
 * Reconcile refuses to delete images without a row when there are more of them than both of these:
 * a database restored from an older snapshot has rows missing for every image posted since, and
 * those images must not go. MEDIA_RECONCILE=force overrides it once the operator has checked.
 */
export const RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHANS = 50;
export const RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE = 0.02;

export interface SweepReport {
  finalized: number;
  timedOut: number;
  expired: number;
  withdrawn: number;
  orphans: number;
  /** Orphan images the reconcile pass refused to delete. */
  refused: number;
}

/**
 * Housekeeping that no request triggers. It is a plain function of the clock, so tests call it
 * with whatever time they need. Every step is safe to repeat and safe to run next to live traffic.
 */
export async function sweep(deps: MediaDeps, now: Date, options: { reconcile: boolean }): Promise<SweepReport> {
  const report: SweepReport = { finalized: 0, timedOut: 0, expired: 0, withdrawn: 0, orphans: 0, refused: 0 };

  // 1. Results nobody asked for: the composer was closed, or the post was written from another device.
  for (const id of await deps.repo.processingIds()) {
    if (await finalize(deps, id)) report.finalized++;
  }

  // 2. Uploads the worker never answered, because it was down or the file killed it three times.
  const stale = await deps.repo.failStale(new Date(now.getTime() - PROCESSING_TIMEOUT_MS));
  // 3. Uploads nobody posted.
  const expired = await deps.repo.deleteUnattachedBefore(new Date(now.getTime() - UNATTACHED_TTL_MS));
  report.timedOut = stale.length;
  report.expired = expired.length;
  for (const id of [...stale, ...expired]) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
  await deps.files.requestDeletion([...stale, ...expired]);

  // 4. Deletions that are owed: rows the account's purge or the disposal deleted whose request was never written (the
  //    process stopped after the commit, or the request failed), asked for now; and the notes of rows that are still
  //    there, forgotten once they are stale. Every pass, so a request that could not be written is retried within
  //    thirty seconds of the volume taking writes again, however many files it names: these are known deletions, not
  //    orphans, and the reconcile pass below never has to judge them.
  await requestOwed(deps, now.getTime());

  // 5. Deletion requests the worker has carried out, once they are old enough to have covered late writes.
  for (const { id, ageMs } of await deps.files.deletionRequestAges(now.getTime())) {
    if (ageMs < DELETION_GRACE_MS || (await deps.files.imageRemains(id))) continue;
    await deps.files.withdrawDeletion(id);
    report.withdrawn++;
  }

  // 6. What a crash between a commit and a file operation left behind, and the files of deleted
  //    accounts, whose rows went by cascade.
  if (options.reconcile && deps.reconcileMode !== "off") {
    const nowMs = now.getTime();
    const stored = await deps.files.storedImages(nowMs);
    const images = stored.filter((entry) => entry.ageMs > ORPHAN_AGE_MS).map((entry) => entry.id);
    const uploads = (await deps.files.storedUploads(nowMs)).filter((entry) => entry.ageMs > ORPHAN_AGE_MS).map((entry) => entry.id);
    const known = await deps.repo.existing([...new Set([...images, ...uploads])]);
    const orphanImages = images.filter((id) => !known.has(id));
    const orphanUploads = uploads.filter((id) => !known.has(id));
    for (const id of orphanUploads) await deps.files.discardUpload(id);
    const tooMany = orphanImages.length > RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHANS && orphanImages.length > stored.length * RECONCILE_MAX_ORPHAN_SHARE;
    if (tooMany && deps.reconcileMode !== "force") {
      report.refused = orphanImages.length;
      report.orphans = orphanUploads.length;
      deps.log.error(
        { images: orphanImages.length, stored: stored.length },
        "media: reconcile refused to delete this many images without a row. If the database was restored from an older snapshot, restore the store from the same one; if the images are really orphans, set MEDIA_RECONCILE=force for one pass",
      );
    } else {
      await deps.files.requestDeletion(orphanImages);
      report.orphans = orphanImages.length + orphanUploads.length;
      if (report.orphans > 0) deps.log.warn({ images: orphanImages.length, uploads: orphanUploads.length }, "media: removed files that had no row");
    }
  }
  return report;
}

/**
 * The sweeper as a job: one instance at a time, rounds never overlapping, the lock refreshed while a
 * long reconcile runs. The reconcile marker is a second key that simply expires every ten minutes.
 */
export function createSweeper(deps: MediaDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  let last: SweepReport | null = null;
  const job = createJob({
    name: "media-sweeper",
    intervalMs: SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS,
    lockTtlMs: SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS,
    lock,
    log: deps.log,
    run: async () => {
      const reconcile = await lock.acquire("job:media-sweeper:reconcile", "due", RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS);
      last = await sweep(deps, deps.now(), { reconcile });
    },
  });
  return {
    /** One round now: the report, or null when another instance holds the lock or a round is still in flight. */
    async round(): Promise<SweepReport | null> {
      last = null;
      return (await job.round()) === "ran" ? last : null;
    },
    /** Sweeps every thirty seconds until the returned function is called. */
    start: job.start,
  };
}
```

```ts
  type OutcomeLineRow,
  type UrgentItemRow,
} from "./repo";
import { sendStatement } from "./statement";

/**
 * The dispatch job (3c design, sections 7.8 and 7.12): every ten minutes it repeats the staff alerts that are still due,
 * runs the daily release once its hour has come, sends the receipts and statements a relay failure left pending, mails
 * each address and account one update of the outcomes released to it, and gives up what stayed unsent for five days.
 *
 * A round runs its steps in the order 5, 3, 1, 2, 4, 6 of the design's list: the alerts first, and the daily release,
 * which writes only to the databases, before any mail, so it never waits behind a relay. Every step runs in a try of its
 * own, and so does every mail: a failure is logged with the step and the row's id, never an address, and leaves the row
 * as it was, so a row that keeps failing never stops the alerts, the release or another row's mail. It stays pending
 * until the last step gives it up.
 *
 * Every time the job compares is its own clock's (`deps.now()`), handed to the database as a parameter, so one clock
 * decides what is fifteen minutes or five days old, and a test can move it.
 */

const MINUTE_MS = 60_000;
const DAY_MS = 24 * 60 * MINUTE_MS;

/** The job's name: its lock is `job:moderation-dispatch`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const DISPATCH_JOB = "moderation-dispatch";
/** The time between the end of one round and the start of the next. */
export const DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * MINUTE_MS;
/** A receipt, a statement and an urgent item are the job's once they are this old: until then the request that made them is still at work on them. */
const DUE_AFTER_MS = 15 * MINUTE_MS;
/** How many pending receipts one round sends. */
const RECEIPTS_PER_ROUND = 100;
/**
 * How many suspect cases one round asks the media module what they reach: one query a case, and a report of child sexual
 * abuse material needs no account, so a flood of them could hold the round's first step for minutes. The oldest cases
 * are read first; any beyond this count as calling, unread, which only repeats an alert that a case read later may ask for
 * anyway.
 */
export const URGENT_REACH_PER_ROUND = 200;
/** How long a cut-off's marker is kept: two days, so a marker is still there for every round of its own day. */
const MARKER_TTL_MS = 2 * DAY_MS;
/** How long the question "is the marker set?" holds the key when the process dies between asking and letting go. */
const MARKER_PROBE_MS = 30_000;

/** The key and the window of the queue-age alert. */
export const WAITING_ALERT_KEY = "moderation-waiting";
export const WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS = DAY_MS;

/** A round's cut-off: the latest dispatch hour (UTC) at or before the round's start. */
export function cutoffOf(start: Date, hour: number): Date {
  const today = Date.UTC(start.getUTCFullYear(), start.getUTCMonth(), start.getUTCDate(), hour);
  return new Date(today <= start.getTime() ? today : today - DAY_MS);
}

/**
 * The marker of a cut-off's release, by the cut-off's day and hour. Because the key holds the hour, a changed dispatch
 * hour gives a cut-off whose release has not run. It lives beside the jobs' locks, which a restore of the database does
 * not bring back: the README's restore steps delete the markers.
 */
export const dispatchMarkerKey = (cutoff: Date) => `moderation-dispatched:${cutoff.toISOString().slice(0, 13)}`;

/** What one round did, for its log line and for the tests. */
export interface DispatchReport {
  /** The urgent lane's repeat: what became of the alert, or "none" when no item still calls for someone. */
  urgent: "sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "nothing_waiting" | "none";
  /** The queue-age alert: what became of it, or "none" when no case is past its time. */
  waiting: "sent" | "throttled" | "unsent" | "none";
  /** How many items the daily release changed, or null when it did not run in this round. */
  released: number | null;
  /** Whether the cut-off's release, both halves, has finished: before this round or in it. */
  marked: boolean;
  /** Whether this round ran the release to its end and wrote the cut-off's marker itself: the daily round. */
  daily: boolean;
  /** The receipts and the statements whose result this round recorded. */
  receipts: number;
  statements: number;
  /** The addresses' contacts and the accounts whose update the relay took. */
  outcomeMails: number;
  givenUp: { receipts: number; authorMails: number; outcomes: number };
}

/** What a mail's result is recorded as; nothing is recorded where the relay could not take the mail, so the next round sends it again. */
const RECORDED: Record<NotifierUpdateResult | AccountMailResult, MailState | null> = {
  sent: "sent",
  suppressed: "suppressed",
  no_address: "no_address",
  // A contact the janitor has forgotten has no address any more.
  forgotten: "no_address",
  // The relay refused the address for good: no later try changes that.
  refused: "failed",
  unavailable: null,
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 5: the alerts

/**
 * Whether an unanswered item of the urgent lane still calls for someone (3c design, section 7.12), in its three cases.
 *   1. A suspect item whose case reaches an image that is still served: until a choice not to seal is recorded on the
 *      case after the item arrived, and then only while no post with a served image was created after the newest such
 *      choice. Nothing else ends it short of the item's answer: after a note, a withhold or a field reset some reader, the
 *      uploader included, is still served the images. A seal ends it by leaving no served image.
 *   2. A suspect item whose case reaches no served image: until a decision taken while deciding, a note or a recorded
 *      choice not to seal comes after the item arrived.
 *   3. Any other item: while no decision taken while deciding came after it and, when the case is about an account or its
 *      post is not visible, no note did either. On a visible post a note never ends it: the post is withheld or decided.
 * The two times of case 1 are compared to the millisecond, and a post created in the same millisecond as the recorded
 * choice counts as created after it: the alert errs on the side of repeating.
 */
export function stillCalls(item: UrgentItemRow, reach: { served: number; newestServedAt: Date | null } | null): boolean {
  if (item.suspect) {
    if (reach === null) throw new Error("a suspect item is judged by what its case reaches");
    if (reach.served > 0) {
      if (!item.declinedAfter || item.newestDeclinedMs === null) return true;
      return reach.newestServedAt !== null && reach.newestServedAt.getTime() >= item.newestDeclinedMs;
    }
    return !(item.interimAfter || item.noteAfter || item.declinedAfter);
  }
  const noteCounts = item.targetType === "account" || item.postHidden;
  return !item.interimAfter && !(noteCounts && item.noteAfter);
}

/**
 * The open cases that hold an unanswered item of the urgent lane which is older than 15 minutes and still calls for
 * someone. What a case reaches is read once for a case, and only for a case that holds a suspect item, for at most
 * `limit` cases, the oldest first. An alert fails open: a case whose reach cannot be read counts as calling, and the
 * failure is logged with the case's id, so one case that keeps failing never silences the lane; so does a suspect case
 * beyond the limit, unread.
 */
export async function casesCalling(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">, now: Date, limit = URGENT_REACH_PER_ROUND): Promise<string[]> {
  const items = await urgentItems(deps.apiDb, new Date(now.getTime() - DUE_AFTER_MS));
  const reaches = new Map<string, { served: number; newestServedAt: Date | null }>();
  const calling = new Set<string>();
  // Every read counts toward the limit, one that fails too.
  let reads = 0;
  for (const item of items) {
    if (calling.has(item.caseId)) continue;
    let reach = reaches.get(item.caseId) ?? null;
    if (item.suspect && reach === null) {
      if (reads >= limit) {
        calling.add(item.caseId);
        continue;
      }
      reads++;
      try {
        reach = await deps.media.reach({ type: item.targetType, id: item.targetId });
      } catch (err) {
        deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "urgent", caseId: item.caseId }, "moderation-dispatch: what a case reaches could not be read; the case counts as calling");
        calling.add(item.caseId);
        continue;
      }
      reaches.set(item.caseId, reach);
    }
    if (stillCalls(item, reach)) calling.add(item.caseId);
  }
  return [...calling];
}

/** The urgent lane's repeat: while a case still calls, the alert is sent again under the key and window of the first one. */
async function repeatUrgent(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<DispatchReport["urgent"]> {
  if ((await casesCalling(deps, now)).length === 0) return "none";
  return alertUrgentLane(deps);
}

/**
 * The queue-age alert, at most once a day: per lane the cases past its response time with the oldest one's time, and the
 * open cases that have held a measure taken while deciding for more than a day, whose author cannot appeal it.
 */
async function alertWaiting(deps: ModerationDeps, now: Date): Promise<DispatchReport["waiting"]> {
  const waiting = await waitingCases(deps.apiDb, now);
  if (waiting.lanes.length === 0 && waiting.interim === 0) return "none";
  return staffAlert(deps, WAITING_ALERT_KEY, WAITING_ALERT_WINDOW_MS, { template: "moderation_waiting", lanes: waiting.lanes, interim: waiting.interim });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 3: the daily release

/**
 * Whether the marker is set. The lock a job runs under is also the store of its markers, and it can only take a key or
 * let it go: the question takes the key for a moment, which fails when the marker is there, and lets it go again. A
 * process that dies in between leaves the key for half a minute, not for the marker's two days.
 */
async function markerSet(lock: JobLock, key: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const probe = randomBytes(16).toString("hex");
  if (!(await lock.acquire(key, probe, MARKER_PROBE_MS))) return true;
  await lock.release(key, probe);
  return false;
}

/**
 * The daily release, until the cut-off's marker is set. (a) The database releases every item answered before the cut-off
 * and every changed outcome. (b) Every contact whose notice is still owed something is kept for another six months. The
 * marker is set once both have finished, so a round that fails in between runs the step again: the release then releases
 * nothing new, and no outcome mail goes before (b) has moved each contact's day.
 *
 * When the marker cannot be asked for, the step runs: it only repeats what a finished release leaves as it is. The round
 * is the daily one only when its own write of the marker was accepted. A marker that could not be written is logged, and
 * the next round that can write it is the daily one: a receipt that rides alone goes out once a day, never once a round.
 */
async function dailyRelease(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock, now: Date, report: DispatchReport): Promise<void> {
  const cutoff = cutoffOf(now, deps.config.MODERATION_DISPATCH_HOUR);
  const key = dispatchMarkerKey(cutoff);
  try {
    if (await markerSet(lock, key)) {
      report.marked = true;
      return;
    }
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker could not be read; the release runs again");
  }
  report.released = await releaseOutcomes(deps.apiDb, cutoff);
  const owed = await contactsOwed(deps.apiDb);
  if (owed.length > 0) await deps.auth.forgetNotifierAfter(owed, appealDeadline(now));
  report.marked = true;
  try {
    report.daily = await lock.acquire(key, "done", MARKER_TTL_MS);
    if (!report.daily) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker was not taken; the next round runs the release again");
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: "release" }, "moderation-dispatch: the release's marker could not be set; the next round runs the release again");
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 4: the outcome mails

/**
 * One line of the daily update, from a released item (3c design, section 7.8, step 4, and section 5). The outcome's words
 * are the contracts' one composition, with the scope the status page gives the same item; the other fields say which of
 * the mail's sentences go with the line.
 */
export function updateLine(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "config">, row: OutcomeLineRow): NoticeUpdateLine {
  const outcome = row.shownOutcome as ItemOutcome;
  const noAction = outcome === "no_violation" || outcome === "not_evident";
  let scope: OutcomeWordsInput["scope"] = null;
  if (row.targetType === "account") scope = row.suspect || row.sealed ? "account_suspect" : "account";
  else if (row.hasCase && !row.suspect && row.quotes) scope = "quote";
  // "No action for now": decided while nobody could open the post's images, on an item about a post that is not itself suspect.
  const unseen = noAction && row.decisionUnseen && row.targetType === "post" && !row.suspect;
  let rule: OutcomeWordsInput["rule"] = null;
  if (outcome === "restricted_rule") {
    // The rule in the wording of the rulebook the decision was made under.
    const found = row.ruleId === null || row.rulesVersion === null ? undefined : getRule(row.ruleId, row.rulesVersion);
    if (!found) throw new Error("the item's restriction names no rule of a rulebook korbat holds");
    rule = { id: found.id, title: found.title };
  }
  return {
    ref: row.ref,
    item: row.position,
    link: itemLink(deps, row),
    outcome: outcomeWords({ outcome, rule, suspect: row.suspect, sealed: row.sealed, unseen, noEffect: row.noEffect, scope }),
    reexamination: row.reexamines,
    changed: row.changed,
    // Only a moderator's decision to take no action can be examined again, once; an answer given with the images out of
    // sight does not spend that, also when it answered a re-examination.
    reexaminable: row.byDecision && noAction && !row.reexamined && (!row.reexamines || unseen),
    unseen,
    automatic: !row.hasCase,
  };
}

/** The log line of a mail that did not go: a relay that could not take it is expected and tried again; anything else is a fault to read. */
function logUnsent(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "log">, err: unknown, step: string, row: Record<string, string | string[]>): void {
  if (err instanceof MailUnavailable) deps.log.warn({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step, ...row }, "moderation-dispatch: a mail was not sent; it stays pending for the next round");
  else deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step, ...row }, "moderation-dispatch: a row failed and was left as it was; the round goes on");
}

/**
 * The outcome mails: every released item whose mail is pending, whichever round released it.
 *   - Signed out, the lines go by contact to the auth module, which alone knows which contacts share an address and sends
 *     each address one update. A receipt the 24-hour cap folded rides with its contact's lines; in the daily round a
 *     contact with a folded receipt and nothing else is passed too, so its address gets an update of receipts alone. In
 *     later rounds a folded receipt goes only with its own contact's retried lines, so an address gets one update a day.
 *   - Signed in, they go as one update per account. An item whose reporter was forgotten has nobody to mail.
 * Each line and each carried receipt records its result only while it is still pending. Where the relay could not take a
 * mail nothing is recorded, and the next round sends it again. The rows a mail's result is recorded on are taken before
 * it is sent, in the transaction that records it (beginMailRecord): a database that cannot write refuses that, and
 * nothing is sent, so a line is never mailed round after round for want of a record. The signed-out updates are one call
 * to the auth module, which groups the contacts by address, so their rows are taken and recorded in one transaction,
 * each part's record in a savepoint of its own; each account's update has a transaction of its own.
 */
async function outcomeMails(deps: ModerationDeps, report: DispatchReport): Promise<void> {
  const q = deps.apiDb;
  const rows = await pendingOutcomeLines(q);
  const folded = new Map<string, NoticeRow>((await foldedReceipts(q)).map((notice) => [notice.contactId!, notice]));

  // One part for each contact, which is one notice; one list for each account.
  const byContact = new Map<string, { ref: string; items: string[]; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }>();
  const byAccount = new Map<string, { items: string[]; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }>();
  const nobody: string[] = [];
  for (const row of rows) {
    let line: NoticeUpdateLine;
    try {
      line = updateLine(deps, row);
    } catch (err) {
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { itemId: row.id });
      continue;
    }
    if (row.contactId !== null) {
      const part = byContact.get(row.contactId) ?? { ref: row.ref, items: [], lines: [] };
      part.items.push(row.id);
      part.lines.push(line);
      byContact.set(row.contactId, part);
    } else if (row.reporterId !== null) {
      const update = byAccount.get(row.reporterId) ?? { items: [], lines: [] };
      update.items.push(row.id);
      update.lines.push(line);
      byAccount.set(row.reporterId, update);
    } else {
      nobody.push(row.id);
    }
  }

  // Signed out. The parts keep the order of their notices, so an address's update lists them as they were sent.
  const parts: NotifierUpdatePart[] = [];
  const carried = new Map<string, NoticeRow>();
  const withReceipt = async (contactId: string, part: { ref: string; lines: NoticeUpdateLine[] }): Promise<void> => {
    const notice = folded.get(contactId);
    if (!notice) {
      parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines });
      return;
    }
    try {
      const receipt = await receiptMessage(deps, notice);
      carried.set(contactId, notice);
      parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines, receipt: { ref: receipt.ref, receivedAt: receipt.receivedAt, items: receipt.items } });
    } catch (err) {
      // The receipt could not be built: the lines go without it, and it waits for the next daily round.
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { intakeId: notice.id });
      if (part.lines.length > 0) parts.push({ contactId, ref: part.ref, lines: part.lines });
    }
  };
  for (const [contactId, part] of byContact) await withReceipt(contactId, part);
  if (report.daily) {
    for (const [contactId, notice] of folded) if (!byContact.has(contactId)) await withReceipt(contactId, { ref: notice.ref, lines: [] });
  }
  if (parts.length > 0) {
    // A transaction that fails before its mail (its rows could not be taken) has sent nothing; the round goes on.
    await q.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await beginMailRecord(tx);
      // Every line's row and every carried receipt's notice, before anything is sent; what another sender recorded
      // meanwhile is left out of the mail.
      const locked = await lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx, [...byContact.values()].flatMap((part) => part.items));
      const sending: NotifierUpdatePart[] = [];
      for (const part of parts) {
        const notice = carried.get(part.contactId);
        if (notice && !(await lockPendingReceipt(tx, notice.id, true))) carried.delete(part.contactId);
        const items = byContact.get(part.contactId)?.items ?? [];
        const lines = part.lines.filter((_, index) => locked.has(items[index]!));
        const receipt = carried.has(part.contactId) ? part.receipt : undefined;
        if (lines.length > 0 || receipt) sending.push({ contactId: part.contactId, ref: part.ref, lines, ...(receipt ? { receipt } : {}) });
      }
      if (sending.length === 0) return;
      let results = new Map<string, NotifierUpdateResult>();
      try {
        results = await deps.auth.mailNotifierUpdates(sending);
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contacts: String(sending.length) });
      }
      for (const part of sending) {
        const state = RECORDED[results.get(part.contactId) ?? "unavailable"];
        if (state === null) continue;
        try {
          await tx.transaction(async (sp) => {
            await recordOutcomeMails(sp, (byContact.get(part.contactId)?.items ?? []).filter((id) => locked.has(id)), state);
            const notice = carried.get(part.contactId);
            if (notice) await recordCarriedReceipt(sp, notice.id, state);
          });
          if (state === "sent") report.outcomeMails++;
        } catch (err) {
          logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contactId: part.contactId });
        }
      }
    }).catch((err: unknown) => logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { contacts: String(parts.length) }));
  }

  // Signed in: one update per account, through the account's own address, each in a transaction of its own.
  for (const [accountId, update] of byAccount) {
    try {
      await q.transaction(async (tx) => {
        await beginMailRecord(tx);
        const locked = await lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx, update.items);
        const lines = update.lines.filter((_, index) => locked.has(update.items[index]!));
        if (lines.length === 0) return;
        const state = RECORDED[await deps.auth.mailAccount(accountId, { template: "notice_update", lines })];
        if (state === null) return;
        await recordOutcomeMails(tx, update.items.filter((id) => locked.has(id)), state);
        if (state === "sent") report.outcomeMails++;
      });
    } catch (err) {
      // The rows are the items: the account is the reporter, whom no log line names.
      logUnsent(deps, err, "outcomes", { itemIds: update.items });
    }
  }

  // The reporter's link was forgotten with their account: there is nobody to mail.
  if (nobody.length > 0) await recordOutcomeMails(q, nobody, "no_address");
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the round

/**
 * One round. `lock` is the store the job's own lock lives in, where the daily release keeps its markers.
 */
export async function dispatchRound(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock): Promise<DispatchReport> {
  const now = deps.now();
  const report: DispatchReport = { urgent: "none", waiting: "none", released: null, marked: false, daily: false, receipts: 0, statements: 0, outcomeMails: 0, givenUp: { receipts: 0, authorMails: 0, outcomes: 0 } };
  const step = async (name: string, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      deps.log.error({ err, job: DISPATCH_JOB, step: name }, "moderation-dispatch: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };
  const due = new Date(now.getTime() - DUE_AFTER_MS);

  // 5. The alerts, each in a try of its own: a case whose reach cannot be read never holds the queue-age alert back.
  await step("urgent", async () => {
    report.urgent = await repeatUrgent(deps, now);
  });
  await step("waiting", async () => {
    report.waiting = await alertWaiting(deps, now);
  });

  // 3. The daily release.
  await step("release", () => dailyRelease(deps, lock, now, report));

  // 1. The receipts a relay failure left pending. sendReceipt records every result but a relay failure, which it logs
  // and leaves pending; any other fault it throws, and the row is logged here with the step and left as it was.
  await step("receipts", async () => {
    for (const intakeId of await pendingReceipts(deps.apiDb, due, RECEIPTS_PER_ROUND)) {
      try {
        const state = await sendReceipt(deps, intakeId);
        if (state !== "pending" && state !== "none") report.receipts++;
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "receipts", { intakeId });
      }
    }
  });

  // 2. The statements that were not mailed after their decision's commit, as they are mailed there.
  await step("statements", async () => {
    for (const decisionId of await pendingAuthorMails(deps.apiDb, due)) {
      try {
        if ((await sendStatement(deps, decisionId)) !== "none") report.statements++;
      } catch (err) {
        logUnsent(deps, err, "statements", { decisionId });
      }
    }
  });

  // 4. The outcome mails, only once the cut-off's release has finished, so each contact's day was moved before its lines go.
  let outcomesTried = false;
  if (report.marked) {
    await step("outcomes", async () => {
      await outcomeMails(deps, report);
      outcomesTried = true;
    });
  }

  // 6. What stayed unsent for five days is given up, without another attempt. Outcome lines only in a round that tried
  // them, after it, so each is tried at least once even when the daily release kept failing for longer than that.
  await step("give-up", async () => {
    const gone = await giveUpReceiptsAndAuthorMails(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
    report.givenUp.receipts = gone.receipts.length;
    report.givenUp.authorMails = gone.authorMails.length;
    for (const id of gone.receipts) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "receipt", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
    for (const id of gone.authorMails) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "statement", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
    if (!outcomesTried) return;
    const lines = await giveUpOutcomeMails(deps.apiDb, now, RETENTION.mailGiveUpDays);
    report.givenUp.outcomes = lines.length;
    for (const id of lines) deps.log.warn({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, kind: "outcome", id }, "moderation: mail given up");
  });

  // One line for a round that did something, so the day's release and its mails can be found in the log: counts only.
  const gaveUp = report.givenUp.receipts + report.givenUp.authorMails + report.givenUp.outcomes;
  if (report.daily || report.receipts + report.statements + report.outcomeMails + gaveUp > 0 || report.urgent === "sent" || report.waiting === "sent") {
    deps.log.info({ job: DISPATCH_JOB, ...report }, "moderation-dispatch: round");
  }
  return report;
}

/** The job: a round every ten minutes, counted from the end of the one before, on one API instance at a time. */
export function createDispatchJob(deps: ModerationDeps, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: DISPATCH_JOB, intervalMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: DISPATCH_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => dispatchRound(deps, lock) });
}
```

```ts
import { createHash, randomBytes, randomUUID, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";
```
